name: pain.signal
description: Paid-service pain classifier for public small-business posts (W5-PAIN-SIGNALS, Project Make Money). Scores where money is ALREADY being spent on a service, vendor, software, or paid staff role and the buyer is unhappy with it or the work is AI-doable. Input is one post: title plus selftext excerpt. Advisory (calibrated:false) -- it can PASS or ESCALATE but never BLOCK; Mike's 0.8 bar is applied downstream in pain/SIGNALS.csv.

is_business_owner_or_operator.instructions: The author is a small-business owner, partner, practice owner, or operator who decides how the business spends money (or is directly quoting one), not an employee venting, a job seeker, a student, a consumer, or a would-be entrepreneur with no business yet

mentions_paying_for_a_service_or_staff_r.instructions: The post describes money actually being spent (or a paid role being staffed) on an external service, vendor, agency, software subscription, or employee/contractor function: a real budget line, a price, a monthly cost, or a salary/wage

dissatisfaction_or_cost_pain.instructions: How strong is the dissatisfaction, waste, or cost pain expressed about the thing the business pays for?
criteria: No pain; the post is neutral or happy about what they pay for
Mild mention of cost with no complaint
Vague annoyance; nothing specific about the paid thing
Some grumbling; the paid thing is named but not the problem
Concrete complaint about a paid service or paid role
Clear dissatisfaction with specifics: what fails, how often, what it costs them
Dissatisfaction plus a cost figure or quantified waste (dollars, hours, lost customers)
Actively frustrated: considering cancelling, firing, switching, or doing it themselves
Tried alternatives or confronted the vendor; still stuck; cost and failure both quantified
Explicit money-for-nothing pain: paying while the work is late, wrong, missing, or lost them business

ai_could_do_this_work.instructions: How much of the paid work described could AI or automation plausibly do now?
criteria: None of it; purely physical or in-person trade work
Almost none; a single trivial task might be automated
A small admin sliver (reminders, templates) with the core human
Some documentation or record-keeping could be generated
Repetitive office tasks partly automatable (sorting, categorising, standard replies)
A clear desk workflow: scheduling, follow-up, logging, or reporting could run automatically
Phone, email, or message handling is central and describable as a scriptable flow
Structured back-office work: intake, billing, records, review requests, appointment booking
Mostly text, phone, scheduling, or records work an agent could run end to end with human review
The entire paid function is software-shaped (answering, booking, data entry, chasing, reporting) and described in enough detail to automate

service_category.instructions: Which paid service category (budget line) is this pain about? Choose the closest; no_paid_service only when no money is being spent

criteria.answering_intake: Phone answering service, call handling, front desk, receptionist, client intake, missed calls
criteria.bookkeeping_accounting: Bookkeeper, accountant, bookkeeping, reconciliation, monthly close
criteria.billing_insurance: Medical/legal billing, coding, insurance claims, A/R chasing, collections
criteria.marketing_seo_ads: Marketing agency, SEO, paid ads, social media management, email marketing
criteria.reviews_reputation: Review generation, reputation management, ratings monitoring
criteria.website_software: Website, CRM or SaaS subscription, app maintenance, software the business pays for
criteria.it_msp_security: MSP, IT support, helpdesk, cybersecurity, backups
criteria.scheduling_admin: Scheduling, admin assistant, virtual assistant, data entry, paperwork
criteria.hiring_hr_payroll: Recruiting, staffing agencies, HR, payroll service, wages for a role AI could trim
criteria.legal_compliance: Lawyers, compliance consultants, licensing, regulatory paperwork
criteria.coaching_consulting: Coaches, consultants, fractional executives, agencies selling advice
criteria.sales_leadgen: Lead generation, cold outreach, appointment setters, SDR-as-a-service
criteria.equipment_vendor: Equipment leases, vendor contracts, supply ordering, maintenance contracts
criteria.other_paid_service: Real paid-service pain that fits none of the categories above
criteria.no_paid_service: No paid service, vendor, software, or paid role is involved

buyer_industry.instructions: Which industry is the buyer's business in? general_small_business only when nothing more specific is stated

criteria.law: Law firm, legal practice, paralegal services
criteria.healthcare_medical: Medical clinic, private practice, therapy practice, home health, chiropractic
criteria.accounting_cpa: CPA firm, accounting practice, tax preparer, bookkeeping firm
criteria.hvac_plumbing_electrical: HVAC, plumbing, electrical, roofing, mechanical trades
criteria.real_estate_property: Real estate brokerage, property management, leasing, short-term rentals
criteria.restaurant_food: Restaurant, food service, catering, bakery, bar, food truck
criteria.it_msp: Managed IT, MSP, software shop, tech services
criteria.veterinary_pet: Veterinary clinic, pet services, grooming, boarding
criteria.fitness_wellness: Gym, fitness studio, wellness, personal training
criteria.professional_services_other: Consulting, staffing, or professional services not covered above
criteria.general_small_business: No industry is stated or inferable

rules.reason: high-confidence paid-service pain from a buyer
no paid spend in post -- drop from pain corpus
